subject: Post-call: ops bottleneck map & target SLAs (BrightScale)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: ops bottleneck map & target SLAs (BrightScale)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and proposed next steps so we have the same checklist going into the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of pain points you mentioned:
- User-facing generation latency spikes at peak: p95 observed ~1.8–2.4s for single-turn generation; first-token for streaming often delayed >600ms.
- Concurrency bursts during product launches: sustained 80–140 concurrent live sessions with ephemeral spikes to 220.
- Quality trade-offs when moving to aggressive quantization; team wants to avoid regressions in open-domain responses.
- Lack of transparent cost breakdown by route/model; ops cannot correlate token cost to customer usage patterns easily.

Current stack you described:
- In-house Llama2 variant on single-GPU autoscaling groups (K8s + custom controller).
- Nginx ingress + WebSocket streaming layer; custom caching layer for short prefixes.
- S3 for KV-state snapshots; Datadog for traces/metrics.

Success criteria you called out:
- Latency: p95 generation < 500ms for typical 50–100 token responses; first-token for streaming < 200ms under target concurrency.
- Concurrency: predictable throughput for 150 concurrent sessions with <10% CPU/GPU oversubscription penalties.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency attribution per route.

Immediate next steps (agreed on call):
1) I will send a short telemetry sampling request (example metrics and minimal ingest) so your infra can redact sensitive bits and we can run a matching workload. Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (SLA + high-level deployment options).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week with your infra + product + our solutions engineer (Marissa) to run capacity scenarios and discuss KV/prefix caching strategies.
3) Share your current traffic profile (QPS distribution, typical length distribution, peak hours) — Marissa will provide a CSV template.

Proposed time slots (PDT): Tue 8/24 10:30–11:30, Wed 8/25 13:00–14:00, Thu 8/26 09:00–10:00. Tell us which works and who from your infra team will join.

Thanks again — I’ll loop in Marissa on the scheduling thread.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0149
Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brightscale.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops bottleneck map & target SLAs (BrightScale)

Olga —

Appreciate the clear recap. That aligns with what we saw internally; a couple items/questions from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) On the p95 target: the 500ms goal sounds great, but can you clarify whether that target assumes any batching or if it’s per-request single-sample latency? Our UX needs the first-token to arrive quickly for perceived responsiveness (we call out <200ms as the threshold).

2) Does Redwood support prefix/KV cache reuse across sessions for the same user to avoid re-computation on repeated prompts? We currently have an interim cache but it’s not shared across pods.

3) Cost model question: for Dedicated deployments, what visibility can we get into per-route token cost and model variant fallbacks? Important for our finance team pre-PO.

I attached our current infra diagram (brightscale-current-arch.pdf) and a short sample of QPS by hour for the last two weeks.

We can do Wed 8/25 13:00–14:00 — I’ll bring our infra lead, Priya, and one engineer from product.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightScale Analytics
Attachment: brightscale-current-arch.pdf

On Aug 21, 2026, at 3:10 PM, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:

> 
> Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and proposed next steps so we have the same checklist going into the technical deep-dive: 
> ...
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops bottleneck map & target SLAs (BrightScale)

Thanks Jordan — great, Wed 8/25 13:00–14:00 (PDT) is locked. I’ve added Marissa (solutions engineer) to run the traffic-simulation checklist and the CSV template she mentioned will be in a follow-up.

Quick answers while we prep the deep-dive: 
- SLA targets: our p95 guidance (sub-500ms) is for single-sample requests with conservative batching; we’ll model both no-batch and aggressive-batch scenarios in the deep-dive. First-token streaming latency <200ms is achievable with prefix caching + optimized WebSocket peers in most Dedicated configurations.
- Prefix/KV cache: yes — Redwood supports shared KV/prefix caching across serving instances for compatible model variants; we'll demonstrate how that reduces duplicate decode work in the demo.
- Cost visibility: Dedicated gives per-route and per-model unit economics exported to the console, and we can provide a short export format for your finance team ahead of any PO.

Action items I’ll take before Wed:
- Marissa to send CSV template + telemetry sample request (by EOD Monday).
- I’ll upload a short HubSpot summary and add the meeting link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/BS-4479
- We’ll prepare a small benchmark matrix covering 50-token and 200-token responses under 50/150/220 concurrent sessions.

If anything changes on your side (attendees or timing) tell us and we’ll accommodate. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Olga
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf
